page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations. In performance testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-threaded capabilities, achieving top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression. Multi-core performance, such as the Geekbench multi-core score of 8819.0 and stress-ng multi-core score of 8777.46, aligns with average tier expectations for this resource class.

Memory bandwidth tests show a cached read speed of 688.9 GB/sec, which drops to 70.65 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, highlighting a performance tradeoff when working with datasets that exceed the 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is suited for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, text processing, and lightweight web serving. However, the 16 GB memory limit and weak text generation speeds on larger models make it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale language model inference.
